root_cause.text: The hackrf driver frees its private device structure via kfree() in the probe error path after the V4L2 device has been registered, but without waiting for already-opened file descriptors to release their references, leading to use-after-free and double-free when those file descriptors later access or release the freed memory.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message detail the race condition where CPU1 opens the device after registration, then CPU0's probe error path calls kfree() on the same memory, while CPU1 subsequently uses the device via ioctl (use-after-free) and later closes it, triggering a second kfree() in the release handler (double-free). The patch replaces v4l2_device_unregister() and the implicit kfree with v4l2_device_put() and returns without freeing, ensuring that only the release() path frees the structure after all references are gone.
